subject: reasoning
question: A, B, C, D, J, K and L are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. Only four people sit between C and J when counted from the right of C. C sits third to the left of B. A sits third to the left of D. L is an immediate neighbour of both J and B. How many people sit between K and L when counted from the right of K?
solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, J, K and L are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table.

1) Only four people sit between C and J when counted from the right of C.

2) C sits third to the left of B.

3) A sits third to the left of D.

4) L is an immediate neighbour of both J and B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb22e9825c8ea557bac505618d61ebec1499c3535fcc7d4ea5e72604911af52a.png] 

Thus, There are **Two** people sit between K and L when counted from the right of K

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
